traceability.evidence:
1) Story file exists but acceptance criteria are unchecked: - docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md - All checkboxes (Core Functionality, Backward Compatibility, Pattern Validation, Error Messages, Quality Standards, Integration, Documentation) remain `[ ]`, indicating not marked as completed.
2) valid-annotation-format rule does not support configurable patterns: - src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts - The rule meta has `schema: []`, so it declares no configuration options at all. - `validateStoryAnnotation` uses a hardcoded regex: `const pathPattern = /^docs\/stories\/[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-DEV-[\w-]+\.story\.md$/;` It never reads a pattern from rule options. - `validateReqAnnotation` uses a hardcoded regex: `const reqPattern = /^REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+$/;` It also never reads from configuration. - The `create(context)` function does not inspect `context.options` and contains no references to `storyPathPattern`, `requirementIdPattern`, `storyPathExample`, or `requirementIdExample`. - JSDoc on this rule references stories 005.0 and 008.0 only; there is no @story reference to docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md.
3) No code or tests reference the new configuration fields or this story: - Searches show: - No occurrences of `storyPathPattern` or `requirementIdPattern` in src/ (including src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts). - No occurrences of `010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS` in tests/. - tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts: - Header references only stories 005.0 and 007.0. - All test cases assume the fixed built-in patterns: - Valid/invalid examples use `docs/stories/005.0-DEV-... .story.md` for @story. - Valid/invalid examples use `REQ-...` for @req. - No test passes options into the rule (no `options` field with custom patterns or examples), so configurable behavior is not exercised.
4) Documentation still describes fixed patterns, not configurable ones: - docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md: - Under “Validated patterns” it documents only fixed regexes: - `@story` paths: `^docs/stories/[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-DEV-[\w-]+\.story\.md$` - `@req` identifiers: `^REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+$` - There is no section describing rule options such as `storyPathPattern`, `requirementIdPattern`, `storyPathExample`, or `requirementIdExample`. - No configuration examples are provided matching the use cases in the story (different directories, different requirement prefixes, custom story file formats).
5) No visible integration alignment with valid-story-reference configuration: - eslint.config.js and other configs do not show any options on `traceability/valid-annotation-format` related to patterns or examples. - There is no code demonstrating or wiring up consistency with `storyDirectories` from the valid-story-reference rule.
6) Tests run for this rule reflect only existing behavior: - Command executed: - `npm test -- --runTestsByPath tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts --verbose --runInBand` - Jest invocation output: - `jest --ci --bail --runTestsByPath tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts --verbose --runInBand` - The referenced test file contains only tests for the fixed regex patterns and existing error messages; nothing relates to configurable patterns, regex validation, or example strings.
traceability.notes: Story 010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS is not implemented. The `valid-annotation-format` rule still uses hardcoded regex patterns for @story paths and @req identifiers, exposes no configuration schema (meta.schema is empty), and never reads configuration options from `context.options`. There is no logic to validate custom regex patterns, no support for custom example strings in error messages, and no alignment with `valid-story-reference` configuration. Tests and documentation cover only the fixed patterns and do not reference this story or its new options. Therefore, multiple key acceptance criteria—core functionality (configurable patterns), backward compatibility via defaults, pattern validation, enhanced error messages, quality/schema standards, integration, and documentation—are not met.
